topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing for the lecture series, covering course context, multidisciplinary audience backgrounds, and core learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic, developmental, and cellular foundations of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the biological nature of cancer as a stepwise failure of genetic regulation, cellular differentiation, and tissue architecture, alongside experimental models used to study it.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and histopathological progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the pathological progression of tumors from local basement-membrane invasion to distant metastatic dissemination.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and pathophysiological mechanisms of morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the classification and naming conventions of tumors and explain the physical and systemic mechanisms through which neoplasms cause illness and death.

topics.label: Cancer epidemiology and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine cancer incidence patterns in human populations and compare tumor susceptibility across companion animals and other multicellular taxa.

topics.label: Clinical cancer symptoms and screening modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the clinical presentation of tumors and evaluate various population screening approaches for early cancer detection.

topics.label: Lecture closing and housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing, directing students to revise learning outcomes and look ahead to practical sessions and future lectures.
